A conducting circular loop is rotated about its diameter at a constant angular speed of $100\,\text{rad/s}$ in a magnetic field of 0.5 T perpendicular to the axis of rotation. When the loop is rotated by $30^{\circ}$ from the horizontal position, the induced EMF is 15.4 mV . The radius of the loop is $\_\_\_\_$ mm.
(Take $\pi = \; \frac{22}{7}$ )

A 20 m long uniform copper wire held horizontally is allowed to fall under the gravity $(g=10\,\text{m/s}^2)$ through a uniform horizontal magnetic field of 0.5 Gauss perpendicular to the length of the wire. The induced EMF across the wire when it travells a vertical distance of 200 m is $\_\_\_\_$ mV .
questions.solution:
Concept: a straight rod moving perpendicular to both its own length and the field has motional EMF $\varepsilon = Blv$.
Speed after falling from rest: $v = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{2 \times 10\,\text{m/s}^2 \times 200\,\text{m}} = \sqrt{4000}\,\text{m/s} = 20\sqrt{10}\,\text{m/s}$
Magnetic field: $B = 0.5\,\text{G} = 0.5 \times 10^{-4}\,\text{T}$
The rod is horizontal, the field is horizontal and perpendicular to the rod, and the velocity is vertical. So $B$, $l$ and $v$ are mutually perpendicular.
$\varepsilon = Blv = (0.5 \times 10^{-4}\,\text{T})(20\,\text{m})(20\sqrt{10}\,\text{m/s})$
$\varepsilon = 0.02\sqrt{10}\,\text{V} = 20\sqrt{10}\,\text{mV}$
Answer: (C) $20\sqrt{10}$ mV
